3dsmax_cache.what: 3ds Max's whole user data folders (settings, scripts, plugins config, autoback).
3dsmax_cache.risk: Lost UI settings, scripts and autobackups.
3dsmax_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole data folder.

amd_comgr_cache.what: AMD Code Object Manager's cache of compiled GPU kernels (ROCm/HIP/OpenCL), on by default.
amd_comgr_cache.used_for: Avoids recompiling GPU code between runs; pruned automatically (default cap 30 GB / 75% of disk).
amd_comgr_cache.risk: First GPU-compute run after cleaning recompiles kernels (slower start).
amd_comgr_cache.before_cleaning: Close apps using GPU compute (AI tools, Blender, etc.).
amd_comgr_cache.catalog_concern: AMD documents the Windows default as %LOCALAPPDATA%\cache\comgr; %LOCALAPPDATA%\comgr may be an older location. Consider adding the documented path.

amd_install_manager_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor: a download cache of AMD Software's installer/updater.
amd_install_manager_cache.risk: A re-download if AMD Software repairs or re-installs.
amd_install_manager_cache.before_cleaning: Not during an AMD Software install/update.

android_studio_cache.what: Android Studio's IDE caches (indexes) and its logs.
android_studio_cache.used_for: Indexes speed up the editor; Android Studio rebuilds them on next start. Logs are only for troubleshooting.
android_studio_cache.risk: Slow first start while re-indexing; lost logs. Gradle caches, SDK and emulator images are elsewhere and not touched.
android_studio_cache.catalog_concern: Paths use %APPDATA%\Google\AndroidStudio*, which is the CONFIG folder; Google documents system files (caches, logs) under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\AndroidStudio<version>. The entry likely finds nothing. Never widen it to the whole config folder.

ansible_cache.what: Ansible's local temporary folder on the controller (~/.ansible/tmp).
ansible_cache.used_for: Scratch space for running playbooks; recreated on next run.
ansible_cache.risk: A playbook running at that moment could fail. Ansible does not run natively on Windows (only under WSL), so it is usually absent.

apt_cache.what: Linux APT paths that do not exist on Windows (WSL keeps them inside the distro's virtual disk).
apt_cache.risk: None on Windows; nothing to find.
apt_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'caution'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: the paths are meaningless on Windows; WSL's apt cache is cleaned inside WSL with 'apt clean'.

arcgis_cache.what: Esri's whole data folder (ArcGIS Pro settings, licensing, project data).
arcgis_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole data folder.

atom_cache.what: Atom editor's Chromium HTTP cache (Cache) and temporary blob storage (blob_storage). Atom was discontinued by GitHub in 2022.
atom_cache.used_for: Both are rebuilt by Electron when Atom starts.
atom_cache.risk: None known; slightly slower first start.

autocad_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor at these paths: AutoCAD per-release Cache and Temp folders.
autocad_cache.used_for: Temporary and cache data rebuilt by AutoCAD.
autocad_cache.risk: Slower first use; a crash-recovery file could sit in Temp if AutoCAD is open.
autocad_cache.catalog_concern: AutoCAD's autosave (.sv$) defaults to %TEMP%; make sure no autosave/recovery files are in these folders.

bazaar_cache.what: Bazaar's ~/.bazaar folder: bazaar.conf, authentication.conf and plugins.
bazaar_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: config and credentials, not a cache.

bundler_cache.used_for: Bundler config (may hold source credentials) and installed spec data.
bundler_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: config, not cache.

chocolatey_cache.what: Chocolatey's download cache, packages set aside after a failed install (lib-bad) and Chocolatey's logs.
chocolatey_cache.used_for: Cache avoids re-downloads; lib-bad is a leftover of a failed install; logs record every choco run.
chocolatey_cache.risk: Lost install history/logs for troubleshooting; re-downloads.
chocolatey_cache.before_cleaning: Only when no choco install/upgrade is running.
chocolatey_cache.catalog_concern: Chocolatey's default download cache is %TEMP%\chocolatey unless cacheLocation is set. Never touch lib\ (installed packages).

clang_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor at these exact paths. Clang's implicit module cache defaults to a 'clang\ModuleCache' folder in the user cache directory (%LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows).
clang_cache.used_for: Precompiled modules are rebuilt on the next compile.
clang_cache.catalog_concern: Listed subfolders (\.cache\clang, clang\Cache) may not match the real ModuleCache path.

claude_cli_cache.what: Claude Code's per-project MCP server logs (observed here: mcp-logs-*\*.jsonl, 402 KB).
claude_cli_cache.used_for: Diagnostics for MCP server connections; new logs are written each session.
claude_cli_cache.catalog_concern: Conversation history and settings are in %USERPROFILE%\.claude, not here.

clion_cache.what: CLion's caches (project indexes, file-system snapshot) and its log files.
clion_cache.used_for: Caches speed up code navigation and search; after deletion the IDE re-indexes every project on next open, which can take minutes. Logs are only for troubleshooting.
clion_cache.risk: Slow first open and high CPU while re-indexing; old logs needed for a bug report are lost. Settings and plugins are not in these folders.
clion_cache.catalog_concern: Paths look in %APPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE>\caches and \logs, but JetBrains documents %APPDATA% as the CONFIG directory; caches and logs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE><version> (logs in its \log). The entry likely finds nothing. Point it at %LOCALAPPDATA% caches/log subfolders only, never the config or whole system folder (Local History).

cmake_cache.what: Not documented as a cache: ~/.cmake holds the CMake user package registry (~/.cmake/packages on non-Windows).
cmake_cache.used_for: Lets find_package locate locally built packages.
cmake_cache.risk: find_package may stop finding locally built projects.
cmake_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'caution'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: registry, not build output.

cocoapods_cache.what: CocoaPods spec repos and pod cache (macOS tool; paths are mac-style).
cocoapods_cache.used_for: Rebuilt by 'pod setup'/'pod install' -- but not relevant on Windows.
cocoapods_cache.risk: Re-download; on Windows nothing should be there.
cocoapods_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'caution'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: ~/.cocoapods also holds repo config; not a Windows tool anyway.

codeblocks_cache.what: Code::Blocks' default configuration profile (default.conf, global variables).
codeblocks_cache.risk: Lost IDE settings and global compiler variables.
codeblocks_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: it is the settings profile.

composer_cache.what: PHP Composer's cache of downloaded package zips and repository metadata.
composer_cache.used_for: Speeds up installs; re-downloaded on demand ('composer clear-cache').
composer_cache.catalog_concern: Composer's Windows default is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Composer; %USERPROFILE%\.composer\cache is the Unix-style path and likely matches nothing.

conan_cache.what: The whole Conan home (~/.conan): remotes, profiles, settings and package data.
conan_cache.risk: Lost remotes/profiles/credentials; rebuild of all packages.
conan_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole home. Only ~/.conan\data (Conan 1) or ~/.conan2\p (Conan 2) are package caches, still costly to rebuild.

curl_cfgs_cache.used_for: User configuration (may contain credentials or proxy settings).
curl_cfgs_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: a config file, not a cache.

darcs_cache.what: Darcs ~/.darcs folder (preferences, possibly a global cache).
darcs_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'caution'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: mixed config.

datagrip_cache.what: DataGrip's caches (project indexes, file-system snapshot) and its log files.
datagrip_cache.used_for: Caches speed up code navigation and search; after deletion the IDE re-indexes every project on next open, which can take minutes. Logs are only for troubleshooting.
datagrip_cache.risk: Slow first open and high CPU while re-indexing; old logs needed for a bug report are lost. Settings and plugins are not in these folders.
datagrip_cache.catalog_concern: Paths look in %APPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE>\caches and \logs, but JetBrains documents %APPDATA% as the CONFIG directory; caches and logs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE><version> (logs in its \log). The entry likely finds nothing. Point it at %LOCALAPPDATA% caches/log subfolders only, never the config or whole system folder (Local History).

docker_desktop_cache.what: Docker Desktop's WSL disk images (all images, containers, volumes), container data, and Kubernetes data.
docker_desktop_cache.risk: Every image, container and named volume (databases!) lost.
docker_desktop_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: use 'docker system prune' or Docker Desktop's clean-up instead.

dotnet_native_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor: %windir%\SystemRuntime is a Windows folder.
dotnet_native_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: Windows system folder.

eclipse_cache.what: Despite the label, the path is Maven's local repository (~/.m2/repository): downloaded libraries, plus artifacts YOU built and installed with 'mvn install'.
eclipse_cache.used_for: Maven and IDEs resolve dependencies from here; downloaded ones are re-fetched on the next build.
eclipse_cache.risk: Large re-download; offline builds fail; locally installed artifacts that exist on no remote are lost until rebuilt.
eclipse_cache.before_cleaning: Close IDEs and stop running Maven builds.
eclipse_cache.catalog_concern: Label/description say Eclipse logs and workspace metadata, but the only path is ~/.m2/repository. Rename to Maven local repository. Also duplicated by java_cache.

emacs_cache.what: Emacs auto-save list (crash-recovery records), installed ELPA packages and package var data.
emacs_cache.used_for: auto-save-list lets recover-session restore edits; elpa is installed packages.
emacs_cache.risk: Lost recovery of unsaved edits; packages must be reinstalled; broken config.
emacs_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: these are recovery data and installed packages, not caches.

flatpak_cache.what: Linux Flatpak data path; not applicable on Windows.
flatpak_cache.used_for: Holds installed Flatpak apps on Linux.
flatpak_cache.risk: On Linux, removes installed apps; on Windows nothing to find.
flatpak_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: installed apps, and not a Windows path.

fork_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor: a ForkLogs folder holding Fork's log files.
fork_cache.catalog_concern: Fork's own data is in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Fork; this entry only touches the logs folder, which is fine.

fusion360_cache.what: Fusion's whole data folders, including the offline cache of cloud designs.
fusion360_cache.used_for: Local copies of designs, some possibly unsynced.
fusion360_cache.risk: Unsynced design changes lost; sign-in lost.
fusion360_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: user data and sign-in.

git_lfs_cache.what: Not a standard Git LFS location; Git LFS stores objects per repository in .git\lfs\objects (or a custom lfs.storage).
git_lfs_cache.used_for: LFS objects are the real content of large files; 'git lfs prune' removes only unreferenced ones.
git_lfs_cache.risk: Files not yet pushed are lost forever.
git_lfs_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: use 'git lfs prune'.

gitkraken_cache.what: GitKraken's whole app data (profiles, account sign-in, settings).
gitkraken_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole data folder with sign-ins.

goland_cache.what: GoLand's caches (project indexes, file-system snapshot) and its log files.
goland_cache.used_for: Caches speed up code navigation and search; after deletion the IDE re-indexes every project on next open, which can take minutes. Logs are only for troubleshooting.
goland_cache.risk: Slow first open and high CPU while re-indexing; old logs needed for a bug report are lost. Settings and plugins are not in these folders.
goland_cache.catalog_concern: Paths look in %APPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE>\caches and \logs, but JetBrains documents %APPDATA% as the CONFIG directory; caches and logs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE><version> (logs in its \log). The entry likely finds nothing. Point it at %LOCALAPPDATA% caches/log subfolders only, never the config or whole system folder (Local History).

golang_cache.what: Go's module download cache (pkg\mod\cache) and build cache (go-build).
golang_cache.used_for: Build cache speeds compiles ('go clean -cache'); module cache is re-downloaded ('go clean -modcache').
golang_cache.risk: Slower first build; re-downloads; offline builds fail. Module cache files are read-only and may resist deletion.
golang_cache.before_cleaning: Do not run during a go build.
golang_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog says safe. Build cache is safe; module download cache costs re-download and breaks offline work -- caution fits better. Deleting only cache\ leaves extracted modules under pkg\mod.

gradle_caches_cache.what: Gradle's dependency and build caches, daemon logs/registry, and downloaded Gradle distributions (wrapper\dists).
gradle_caches_cache.used_for: Gradle re-downloads dependencies and distributions on the next build; it also prunes these itself (unused >30 days).
gradle_caches_cache.risk: Long, large first build; offline builds fail; deleting while a daemon runs can break that build.
gradle_caches_cache.catalog_concern: Overlaps java_cache. Never widen to ~/.gradle itself: gradle.properties there can hold credentials/signing keys.

heidisql_cache.what: HeidiSQL's data folder (backups of unsaved query tabs, settings/sessions).
heidisql_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: user data.

hyperv_cache.what: Hyper-V virtual machine configurations, checkpoints and virtual hard disks.
hyperv_cache.risk: Virtual machines and their data destroyed.
hyperv_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: remove VMs/checkpoints through Hyper-V Manager.

hyperv_vmstate_cache.what: Hyper-V's machine data folder, including saved-state (.vsv/.vmrs) files and VM configuration.
hyperv_vmstate_cache.used_for: Saved state is a paused VM's memory.
hyperv_vmstate_cache.risk: VMs lose their saved state or become unregistered.
hyperv_vmstate_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: VM state, managed by Hyper-V.

intellij_cache.what: IntelliJ IDEA's caches (project indexes, file-system snapshot) and its log files.
intellij_cache.used_for: Caches speed up code navigation and search; after deletion the IDE re-indexes every project on next open, which can take minutes. Logs are only for troubleshooting.
intellij_cache.risk: Slow first open and high CPU while re-indexing; old logs needed for a bug report are lost. Settings and plugins are not in these folders.
intellij_cache.catalog_concern: Paths look in %APPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE>\caches and \logs, but JetBrains documents %APPDATA% as the CONFIG directory; caches and logs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE><version> (logs in its \log). The entry likely finds nothing. Point it at %LOCALAPPDATA% caches/log subfolders only, never the config or whole system folder (Local History).

java_cache.what: Maven local repo, Gradle caches and daemon folder, Ivy cache, and the Java Web Start/applet deployment cache.
java_cache.used_for: Build tools re-download dependencies; Java Web Start re-downloads apps.
java_cache.risk: Large re-downloads; offline builds fail; locally installed Maven artifacts lost; a running Gradle daemon can break.
java_cache.before_cleaning: Stop Gradle daemons (gradlew --stop) and close IDEs.
java_cache.catalog_concern: Overlaps eclipse_cache (~/.m2/repository) and gradle_caches_cache (~/.gradle\caches, \daemon) -- same bytes counted twice. %LOCALAPPDATA%\Maven\repository is not a default location.

jetbrains_cache.what: Caches (indexes) and logs of every JetBrains IDE, in one entry.
jetbrains_cache.used_for: Caches speed up code navigation and search; after deletion the IDE re-indexes every project on next open, which can take minutes. Logs are only for troubleshooting.
jetbrains_cache.risk: Slow first open and high CPU while re-indexing; old logs needed for a bug report are lost. Settings and plugins are not in these folders.
jetbrains_cache.catalog_concern: The label says compiler/build artifacts, but these are IDE indexes/logs (not Maven/Gradle). Local/JetBrains contains plugins and caches: target caches or use Invalidate Caches. Roaming/JetBrains is configuration; do not target it. The ProgramData cache path is undocumented. Narrow paths to documented caches; never delete the whole IDE data folder.

kind_cache.what: kind's ~/.kind folder (cluster config and cached data).
kind_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: cluster state, use 'kind delete cluster'.

kubernetes_cache.what: kubectl's cache directory (~/.kube/cache): API discovery data and HTTP responses.
kubernetes_cache.used_for: Speeds up kubectl; rebuilt on the next command.
kubernetes_cache.risk: None known; first command slightly slower. ~/.kube\config (credentials) is not touched.

lazarus_cache.risk: Lost IDE configuration and package list.
lazarus_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole config folder.

lm_studio_cache.what: LM Studio's Electron HTTP cache and its logs. Downloaded models are NOT here (they are under %USERPROFILE%\.lmstudio or .cache\lm-studio).
lm_studio_cache.used_for: Cache is rebuilt by Chromium; logs are diagnostics.
lm_studio_cache.risk: Lost logs; slightly slower first start.
lm_studio_cache.catalog_concern: Description says 'AI model cache' -- misleading; models are elsewhere (good, or this would be many GB of re-download).

logitech_g_hub_cache.what: Logitech G HUB's whole data folders (profiles, macros, settings, sign-in).
logitech_g_hub_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole data folder.

maple_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole data folder.

matlab_cache.what: MathWorks' whole data folders (preferences, add-ons, licence).
matlab_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole data folder.

matlab_full_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: settings folder.

maven_repo_cache.risk: Same as eclipse_cache: re-download, offline builds fail, locally installed artifacts lost.
maven_repo_cache.catalog_concern: Disabled only as a duplicate of eclipse_cache -- right.

maya_cache.what: Maya's whole per-version prefs and scripts folders.
maya_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole data folder.

mercurial_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor: ~/.hg is not a standard Mercurial folder (config is ~/.hgrc / mercurial.ini).
mercurial_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'caution'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: not a known cache.

meson_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor: Meson keeps build data inside each build directory, not ~/.cache/meson.
meson_cache.used_for: If present, any cache would be rebuilt.

minikube_cache.what: The whole minikube home: cluster profiles, certificates, machine disks and the image cache.
minikube_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: only ~/.minikube\cache is a re-downloadable cache; use 'minikube delete'.

msix_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor: Windows' own package-manager and package staging folders.
msix_cache.used_for: Used by Windows while deploying Store/MSIX apps.
msix_cache.risk: Can break app installs/updates in progress.
msix_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: Windows deployment state.

mysql_logs.what: Log files of a local MySQL server in a 'logs' folder under its program folder (error, general, slow-query logs if configured there).
mysql_logs.used_for: Diagnostics; MySQL's default error log is <host>.err in the data directory (usually ProgramData).
mysql_logs.risk: Lost diagnostics; the active log is locked while MySQL runs. If binary logs were placed here, deleting them breaks replication and point-in-time recovery.
mysql_logs.before_cleaning: Stop or flush logs (FLUSH LOGS) first; never delete binlog files by hand (PURGE BINARY LOGS).
mysql_logs.catalog_concern: Not a default MySQL location. Make sure the entry can never match binlog.* or the data directory.

navicat_cache.what: Navicat's data folder (connections, saved queries, possibly passwords).
navicat_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: user data.

net_framework_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor: Framework\*\NGEN folders are not where .NET native images live (they are in %windir%\assembly\NativeImages_*).
net_framework_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: Windows system folder; use 'ngen' itself, never delete.

netbeans_cache.what: NetBeans log files (var\log\messages.log) and cache folders.
netbeans_cache.used_for: Caches (indexes) are rebuilt by rescanning sources at next start; logs are diagnostics.
netbeans_cache.risk: Rescan on next start; lost logs. Settings are in the user directory, not touched.
netbeans_cache.catalog_concern: NetBeans keeps its cache in %LOCALAPPDATA%\NetBeans\Cache\<version>; the Roaming '**\cache' glob may find little. Never widen to the whole Roaming user directory.

npm_cache.what: Download caches of npm (_cacache), Yarn and pnpm's global store.
npm_cache.used_for: Package tarballs reused by installs; re-downloaded on demand. Already-installed node_modules keep working.
npm_cache.risk: Re-downloads; offline installs fail. npm docs say clearing is rarely needed ('npm cache verify' garbage-collects).
npm_cache.before_cleaning: Do not run during an npm/yarn/pnpm install.
npm_cache.catalog_concern: Overlaps pnpm_cache for pnpm stores. pnpm hard-links from its store, so much of it is still used by projects and is not freed.

npp_cache.what: Notepad++ backup folder (unsaved and unnamed tabs from session snapshot) and plugin configuration.
npp_cache.used_for: Backup is how Notepad++ restores unsaved tabs after closing or a crash; plugins\config holds plugin settings.
npp_cache.risk: Permanent loss of unsaved text and plugin settings.
npp_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: backup holds unsaved documents (user data), plugins\config is settings.

nuget_cache.what: NuGet's global packages folder (~/.nuget/packages) and HTTP caches (v3-cache).
nuget_cache.used_for: Restore and builds read packages from global-packages; NuGet re-downloads on the next restore. 'dotnet nuget locals all --clear' is the supported way.
nuget_cache.risk: Builds fail until restored; large re-download; offline machines and private/local feeds may not recover.
nuget_cache.before_cleaning: Close Visual Studio/Rider and stop builds.

nuget_global_packages.what: NuGet's global packages folder: every package version restored on this machine.
nuget_global_packages.used_for: Builds reference packages here directly; restore re-downloads them.
nuget_global_packages.risk: Builds fail until 'dotnet restore'; re-downloads; packages from feeds no longer reachable cannot come back.
nuget_global_packages.before_cleaning: Close Visual Studio/Rider and stop builds.

nvm_caches.what: nvm-windows' root folder: every installed Node.js version plus settings.txt.
nvm_caches.risk: All Node versions and nvm settings lost; node stops working.
nvm_caches.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: installed runtimes.

opencode_desktop_cache.what: Chromium/Electron caches of the OpenCode desktop app: temporary blobs, Dawn WebGPU/Graphite shader caches and the compression-dictionary cache (Shared Dictionary).
opencode_desktop_cache.used_for: All are rebuilt by Chromium on demand.
opencode_desktop_cache.risk: None known; first pages may load a little slower.
opencode_desktop_cache.catalog_concern: Correctly avoids Local Storage, Session Storage, Network and opencode\ (session data). Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache and GrShaderCache exist here too and are equally safe if wanted.

packer_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor: Packer documents plugins under %APPDATA%\packer.d\plugins and its cache as ./packer_cache in the working folder.
packer_cache.used_for: A plugin cache would be re-downloaded by 'packer init'.
packer_cache.catalog_concern: The listed path is not a documented Packer folder and likely matches nothing. Never retarget to packer.d\plugins (installed plugins).

parallels_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: user VMs.

perforce_cache.what: Perforce P4 client folders (settings, connection data; tickets may be nearby).
perforce_cache.used_for: Client configuration and possibly login tickets.
perforce_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: settings/sign-in data.

phpstorm_cache.what: PhpStorm's caches (project indexes, file-system snapshot) and its log files.
phpstorm_cache.used_for: Caches speed up code navigation and search; after deletion the IDE re-indexes every project on next open, which can take minutes. Logs are only for troubleshooting.
phpstorm_cache.risk: Slow first open and high CPU while re-indexing; old logs needed for a bug report are lost. Settings and plugins are not in these folders.
phpstorm_cache.catalog_concern: Paths look in %APPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE>\caches and \logs, but JetBrains documents %APPDATA% as the CONFIG directory; caches and logs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE><version> (logs in its \log). The entry likely finds nothing. Point it at %LOCALAPPDATA% caches/log subfolders only, never the config or whole system folder (Local History).

pip_cache.what: pip's HTTP download cache and the wheels it built from source, plus pip logs.
pip_cache.used_for: Avoids re-downloading and rebuilding; 'pip cache purge' empties it. Installed packages are not here.
pip_cache.risk: Re-downloads and rebuilds of source packages (can be slow); offline installs fail.
pip_cache.before_cleaning: Do not run during a pip install.

pnpm_cache.used_for: pnpm hard-links packages from here into every project's node_modules; re-downloaded when missing.
pnpm_cache.risk: Re-downloads; space shared with projects via hard links is not freed. 'pnpm store prune' is the supported clean-up.
pnpm_cache.before_cleaning: Do not run during a pnpm install.
pnpm_cache.catalog_concern: Current pnpm default on Windows is %LOCALAPPDATA%\pnpm\store, not listed. %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\npm\cache is not a known Windows location.

postgres_logs.what: Not a documented PostgreSQL location: server logs live in the data directory's log\ (pg_log) folder.
postgres_logs.risk: Lost diagnostics. The description mentions pg_xlog/WAL: WAL is NOT a log to clean -- deleting it corrupts the database.
postgres_logs.catalog_concern: Description says 'pg_xlog archive files' -- WAL (pg_xlog/pg_wal) must never be deleted by a cleaner. Remove that wording; keep the path away from any data directory.

pulumi_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor at %APPDATA%\Pulumi; Pulumi's home is ~/.pulumi (credentials.json, plugins, local state).
pulumi_cache.used_for: If it is Pulumi data it includes credentials and possibly local stack state.
pulumi_cache.risk: Sign-out and possibly lost stack state.
pulumi_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: may contain credentials/state.

pycharm_cache.what: PyCharm's caches (project indexes, file-system snapshot) and its log files.
pycharm_cache.used_for: Caches speed up code navigation and search; after deletion the IDE re-indexes every project on next open, which can take minutes. Logs are only for troubleshooting.
pycharm_cache.risk: Slow first open and high CPU while re-indexing; old logs needed for a bug report are lost. Settings and plugins are not in these folders.
pycharm_cache.catalog_concern: Paths look in %APPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE>\caches and \logs, but JetBrains documents %APPDATA% as the CONFIG directory; caches and logs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE><version> (logs in its \log). The entry likely finds nothing. Point it at %LOCALAPPDATA% caches/log subfolders only, never the config or whole system folder (Local History).

pyenv_cache.what: pyenv (Unix) keeps downloaded Python source tarballs in ~/.pyenv/cache; pyenv-win instead uses .pyenv\pyenv-win\install_cache.
pyenv_cache.used_for: Only needed to reinstall a version without downloading.
pyenv_cache.risk: Re-downloads. pyenv-win reportedly uses install_cache during uninstall.
pyenv_cache.catalog_concern: On Windows the listed path is unlikely to exist. Do not retarget it to pyenv-win\versions (installed Pythons).

qt_creator_cache.what: Qt Creator's settings folder (QtProject\QtCreator.ini, kits, sessions) and local data.
qt_creator_cache.used_for: This is configuration, not a cache.
qt_creator_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: QtProject is the settings folder.

resharper_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor at this path ('Unoble' looks like a typo). ReSharper's real caches are under %LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\Transient.
resharper_cache.used_for: Solution caches rebuild when Visual Studio reopens the solution.
resharper_cache.risk: If the folder existed it would be unknown content; re-analysis of solutions after a real cache clear.
resharper_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is not a documented ReSharper cache folder. If re-enabled, target %LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\Transient\*\*\SolutionCaches only.

revitable_cache.what: Revit's family cache, log files and UI cache.
revitable_cache.used_for: Caches are recreated when Revit next opens; logs are diagnostics.
revitable_cache.catalog_concern: Keep CollaborationCache/PacCache out: Autodesk warns they can hold unsynchronised cloud-model changes.

rider_cache.what: Rider's caches (project indexes, file-system snapshot) and its log files.
rider_cache.used_for: Caches speed up code navigation and search; after deletion the IDE re-indexes every project on next open, which can take minutes. Logs are only for troubleshooting.
rider_cache.risk: Slow first open and high CPU while re-indexing; old logs needed for a bug report are lost. Settings and plugins are not in these folders.
rider_cache.catalog_concern: Paths look in %APPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE>\caches and \logs, but JetBrains documents %APPDATA% as the CONFIG directory; caches and logs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE><version> (logs in its \log). The entry likely finds nothing. Point it at %LOCALAPPDATA% caches/log subfolders only, never the config or whole system folder (Local History).

ruby_gems_cache.what: User-installed Ruby gems (~/.gem\gems, specifications) and Bundler's config folder.
ruby_gems_cache.used_for: Installed gems, and ~/.bundle\config can hold private gem-server credentials.
ruby_gems_cache.risk: Projects stop running until reinstalled; lost credentials.
ruby_gems_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: installed gems and config, not a cache. Only ~/.gem\cache would be safe-ish.

rubymine_cache.what: RubyMine's caches (project indexes, file-system snapshot) and its log files.
rubymine_cache.used_for: Caches speed up code navigation and search; after deletion the IDE re-indexes every project on next open, which can take minutes. Logs are only for troubleshooting.
rubymine_cache.risk: Slow first open and high CPU while re-indexing; old logs needed for a bug report are lost. Settings and plugins are not in these folders.
rubymine_cache.catalog_concern: Paths look in %APPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE>\caches and \logs, but JetBrains documents %APPDATA% as the CONFIG directory; caches and logs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE><version> (logs in its \log). The entry likely finds nothing. Point it at %LOCALAPPDATA% caches/log subfolders only, never the config or whole system folder (Local History).

rust_cache.what: Cargo's downloaded crate archives (registry\cache) and their extracted sources (registry\src).
rust_cache.used_for: Cargo re-extracts or re-downloads crates when a build needs them; newer Cargo prunes these itself.
rust_cache.risk: Re-downloads; offline builds fail. Project target\ folders are not touched.
rust_cache.before_cleaning: Do not run during a cargo build.

scoop_bucket_cache.used_for: Lets Scoop reinstall the same version without downloading; 'scoop cache rm *' is the supported clean.
scoop_bucket_cache.risk: Re-download on reinstall. Installed apps (scoop\apps) are not affected.

scoop_cache.catalog_concern: Disabled only as a duplicate -- right.

sdkman_cache.what: SDKMAN! candidates = the installed JDKs/SDKs themselves.
sdkman_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: ~/.sdkman\archives is the download cache, candidates is the installs.

smartgit_cache.what: SmartGit's whole settings folder (preferences, repositories list, credentials).
smartgit_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole settings folder.

sourcetree_cache.what: Sourcetree's whole data (accounts, saved passwords, bookmarks).
sourcetree_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole data folder with sign-ins.

spss_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole data folder.

sql_server_logs.what: SQL Server's LOG folder: ERRORLOG files, SQL Agent logs, default trace (.trc) and system_health (.xel) files.
sql_server_logs.used_for: Diagnostics; SQL Server rotates them (6 by default, more via settings) and sp_cycle_errorlog starts a new one.
sql_server_logs.risk: Lost diagnostic/audit history; the current ERRORLOG is locked. Only rotated ERRORLOG.n files are normally removed.
sql_server_logs.before_cleaning: Cycle the log (sp_cycle_errorlog) and keep the current files.
sql_server_logs.catalog_concern: Real path is MSSQLnn.<instance>\MSSQL\Log, so 'MSSQL*\LOG' may not match. FTData (full-text catalogs) is not a log -- keep it out.

sqlitebrowser_cache.what: DB Browser for SQLite settings folder.
sqlitebrowser_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'caution'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: config, not a cache.

stata_cache.what: Stata's data folder (user ado files, preferences).
stata_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: user data.

sublime_cache.what: Sublime Text's cache (compiled syntaxes), its symbol index database (Index) and logs.
sublime_cache.used_for: Rebuilt on next start; indexing re-runs over open folders.
sublime_cache.risk: Slower first start and re-indexing. Settings and packages are in Packages/Installed Packages, not touched.
sublime_cache.catalog_concern: Sublime Text 4 keeps Cache/Index in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Sublime Text, not %APPDATA%; the Roaming paths only match ST3 or portable-style installs.

subversion_cache.what: Subversion's ~/.subversion folder: config, servers file and the auth folder of saved passwords.
subversion_cache.used_for: Configuration and cached credentials -- not working-copy pristine data (that lives in each .svn).
subversion_cache.risk: Saved SVN logins and settings lost.
subversion_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: auth\ is a sign-in store.

terraform_cache.what: Terraform's shared provider plugin cache (only exists if plugin_cache_dir is configured).
terraform_cache.used_for: Providers are downloaded once and linked/copied into each project's .terraform folder; Terraform never prunes it.
terraform_cache.risk: Re-downloads on next 'terraform init'; projects linked by symlink fail until re-init; offline init fails.
terraform_cache.catalog_concern: On Windows the CLI config dir is %APPDATA% (terraform.d); %USERPROFILE%\.terraform.d\plugin-cache only matches if the user chose it.

tesseract_cache.what: A Tesseract data folder (trained language data).
tesseract_cache.used_for: OCR language models, needed to recognise text.
tesseract_cache.risk: OCR stops working for those languages until re-downloaded.
tesseract_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'caution'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: data files, not cache.

uv_cache.what: uv's cache of downloaded Python packages, built wheels and interpreters.
uv_cache.used_for: uv hard-links files from here into environments; re-downloaded when needed. 'uv cache clean/prune' are the supported commands.
uv_cache.risk: Re-downloads; hard-linked files stay in use (not freed). Environments made with UV_LINK_MODE=symlink BREAK.
uv_cache.before_cleaning: Close running uv processes (uv locks the cache).
uv_cache.catalog_concern: uv docs advise against deleting inside the cache by hand; whole-cache removal is fine except symlink-mode environments.

vcpkg_cache.what: The vcpkg tool's own clone (source\repos\vcpkg): the tool, ports, built packages and installed libraries.
vcpkg_cache.used_for: This is the installation, not a cache.
vcpkg_cache.risk: vcpkg and every library installed through it disappear.
vcpkg_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: only its downloads\ and buildtrees\ subfolders are disposable.

vcredist_cache.what: A folder inside C:\Windows\Installer, the Windows Installer cache.
vcredist_cache.used_for: Windows needs the cached packages to repair, patch and uninstall programs.
vcredist_cache.risk: Programs can no longer be repaired, updated or uninstalled.
vcredist_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: never delete anything under %windir%\Installer by hand.

venv_cache.what: A Python virtual environment at ~/.venv (interpreter link and installed packages).
venv_cache.used_for: A working environment, not a cache.
venv_cache.risk: Anything using that environment breaks until recreated.
venv_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: an environment, not a cache.

vim_cache.what: Vim persistent undo files and swap files.
vim_cache.used_for: Swap files are Vim's crash recovery for unsaved edits; undo files keep undo history across sessions.
vim_cache.risk: Lost recovery of unsaved edits; lost undo history.
vim_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: swap files are the only copy of unsaved edits after a crash.

vmware_cache.what: VMware settings folders and the Virtual Machines folder with VM disks and snapshots.
vmware_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: user VMs.

vscode_cache.what: VS Code's Chromium HTTP cache (Cache), compiled-script cache (Code Cache) and its log files.
vscode_cache.used_for: Electron/Chromium rebuild Cache and Code Cache automatically; logs are only for troubleshooting.
vscode_cache.risk: Slightly slower first start; lost logs. Sign-ins, settings and extensions are not in these folders.
vscode_cache.catalog_concern: The %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\VSCode\... paths are not a VS Code data location (user data is %APPDATA%\Code); they match nothing. Keep it away from Local Storage, Session Storage, Network and User.

vscode_cached_data.what: CachedData holds V8 code caches of VS Code's own scripts; CachedProfilesData caches profile data.
vscode_cached_data.used_for: Speeds up startup; VS Code regenerates both on the next launch.
vscode_cached_data.risk: Slower first launch. None known beyond that.

vscode_cached_extensions.what: Downloaded extension packages (.vsix) VS Code kept after installing or updating extensions.
vscode_cached_extensions.used_for: Kept so an install can be repeated without downloading; installed extensions run from %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions, not from here.
vscode_cached_extensions.risk: A re-download if an extension is reinstalled. Installed extensions keep working.

vscode_dawn_cache.what: Shader caches of Chromium's Dawn WebGPU/Graphite graphics layer inside VS Code.
vscode_dawn_cache.used_for: Compiled GPU shaders reused between launches; recompiled automatically when needed.
vscode_dawn_cache.risk: Brief extra GPU compile time on next start. None known otherwise.

vscode_settings_sync.what: Not documented by the vendor: VS Code writes logs to %APPDATA%\Code\logs, and %APPDATA%\Code\User holds settings, keybindings, snippets and workspace storage.
vscode_settings_sync.used_for: If a User\log folder exists it would only be log output.
vscode_settings_sync.risk: Only logs are targeted, so lost diagnostics. Widening this to User\ would delete settings and unsaved workspace state.
vscode_settings_sync.catalog_concern: Path User\log is not a documented VS Code location and likely matches nothing; the description mentions 'workspace storage cache', which lives in User\workspaceStorage and holds per-workspace state -- do not add it.

vscode_webstorage.what: Chromium's newer storage-bucket area (WebStorage) used by VS Code's web views and extensions.
vscode_webstorage.used_for: Holds web-content storage such as IndexedDB/Cache Storage for buckets; data an extension or webview saved, not a plain cache.
vscode_webstorage.risk: Can lose extension or webview data and sign-in state.
vscode_webstorage.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: WebStorage is site/extension storage, the same class as IndexedDB and Local Storage.

vscodium_cache.what: VSCodium's whole user-data profile and its whole local app folder.
vscodium_cache.used_for: Contains settings, extensions state, Local Storage, sign-ins and caches together.
vscodium_cache.risk: Lost settings, extension state, unsaved backups (Backups folder) and sign-ins.
vscodium_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: the paths are the whole profile. Safe subfolders would be %APPDATA%\VSCodium\Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache, CachedData and logs.

webstorm_cache.what: WebStorm's caches (project indexes, file-system snapshot) and its log files.
webstorm_cache.used_for: Caches speed up code navigation and search; after deletion the IDE re-indexes every project on next open, which can take minutes. Logs are only for troubleshooting.
webstorm_cache.risk: Slow first open and high CPU while re-indexing; old logs needed for a bug report are lost. Settings and plugins are not in these folders.
webstorm_cache.catalog_concern: Paths look in %APPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE>\caches and \logs, but JetBrains documents %APPDATA% as the CONFIG directory; caches and logs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE><version> (logs in its \log). The entry likely finds nothing. Point it at %LOCALAPPDATA% caches/log subfolders only, never the config or whole system folder (Local History).

wget_cache.what: wget's config file (.wgetrc) and HSTS database (.wget-hsts).
wget_cache.used_for: Config; the HSTS list enforces HTTPS for known sites.
wget_cache.risk: Lost config; weaker HTTPS enforcement until relearned.
wget_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'caution'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: config/security state.

whisper_cache.used_for: Downloaded speech models reused by every run.
whisper_cache.risk: Large re-downloads; possible loss of outputs.
whisper_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'caution'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: models and possibly user output.

winget_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor at this path; on this machine %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\winget holds Links and Packages (portable app installs), with no cache or logs folder.
winget_cache.used_for: winget's documented logs are in the App Installer package's LocalState\DiagOutputDir and auto-delete after 7 days.
winget_cache.risk: If cache/logs exist: lost diagnostics only.
winget_cache.catalog_concern: Keep the entry to the cache and logs subfolders: the sibling Packages and Links folders are installed portable apps and their command shims.

wolfram_cache.what: Wolfram's whole data folder (paclets, kernel init, preferences).
wolfram_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole data folder.

workbench_cache.what: MySQL Workbench's data (connections.xml, saved SQL workspaces, history).
workbench_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: user data.

wsl2_cache.what: WSL distros' LocalState (the ext4.vhdx disk holding the whole Linux system and its files), Windows containers data and legacy Lxss.
wsl2_cache.risk: Whole Linux installations and all files inside them lost.
wsl2_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: these are the distros. Microsoft documents shrinking/cleaning inside WSL instead.

wsl2_distro_cache.what: Whole WSL distribution package folders, including ext4.vhdx.
wsl2_distro_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: these are the distros.

wsl_installer_cache.what: WSL distros' LocalState folders -- which hold the ext4.vhdx disk, not installer staging.
wsl_installer_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'caution' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: the description is wrong; LocalState is the distro disk.

zbrush_cache.what: Maxon's whole data folders (ZBrush, Cinema 4D, Redshift, Maxon App).
zbrush_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole vendor folder.

zed_cache.what: Zed editor's whole %APPDATA%\Zed folder (settings, keymap) and a rustup folder under it.
zed_cache.used_for: Holds user configuration, not a cache.
zed_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog safety 'safe' is wrong (should be 'danger'), moot while disabled. Disabling was right: whole config folder.
